description: canonical_bytes(subject) for subject.binary/1 (verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5 + subject.binary/1 §7): the canonical bytes ARE the exact input bytes — byte-identity, opaque, no transformation of any kind. The verifier derives subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes) and the CCCP/1 commitment SHA3-256(ASCII(nonce_hex) || ASCII(subject_local_digest_hex)). These vectors pin the edge cases (empty subject, embedded NUL, leading BOM) so no implementation adds a hidden normalization.
canonicalization: identity: canonical_bytes = exact input bytes; no decode/transcode/normalize/decompress/BOM-strip; embedded NUL preserved; no length limit
commitment_construction: commitment_digest_hex = SHA3-256(ASCII(nonce_hex) || ASCII(subject_local_digest_hex)); all lowercase hex, ASCII concatenation of the hex strings (NOT the binary digests) — CCCP/1 §8.1
must_hold: canonical_bytes is byte-identity: no normalization, transcoding, decompression, BOM stripping, or member reordering
the empty byte sequence is a valid subject; its digest is SHA3-256("")
embedded NUL (0x00) is preserved; no byte is treated as a terminator; there is no length limit
the commitment concatenates the ASCII bytes of the lowercase hex strings, not the decoded 32-byte digests (CCCP/1 §8.1)
